cases.prompt: I keep writing track("github-click") in different components. How should I organize my analytics events?
expectations: Creates one constants/analytics.ts file exporting ANALYTICS_EVENTS constants and an AnalyticsEvent union type.
Requires every call site to use ANALYTICS_EVENTS.GITHUB_CLICK, never an inline string literal.
Notes event names are snake_case and stable — renaming breaks historical dashboards, so treat the catalog as a contract.
Explains the union type makes typos a compile error (e.g. "github-click" vs "github_click").

cases.prompt: One of our analytics providers throws sometimes and it takes down the page. How do I make tracking safe?
expectations: Implements track() as the single entry point that iterates an adapter registry, each adapter call in its own try/catch.
Ensures a failing or absent provider can never throw into the caller or block dispatch to remaining providers.
Makes each adapter guard its provider global and no-op on the server (no window) or when the script is absent.
Keeps the adapter registry exported and mutable so tests can swap in a recording sink to assert dispatch.

cases.prompt: We need to respect GDPR and not send any analytics before the user accepts cookies. Where should that check live?
expectations: Checks consent once at the fan-out boundary — track() early-returns when hasConsent() is false.
Does not duplicate the consent check at every call site.
Gates events, web vitals, and error PII all through the same consent gate.
Defaults consent to false where required and keeps props PII-light (ids/enums, not emails/names).

cases.prompt: My tracked component crashes in tests and during server rendering because there's no analytics provider. How do I fix it?
expectations: Exposes track through a 'use client' context hook, useAnalytics().
Returns a no-op (NOOP context value) when used outside a provider or on the server, so components never throw.
Wraps tracked leaves in thin client components because Server Components can't use the hook.
Keeps the provider render-work-free with a memoized/stable context value so it can mount at the root in SSR/RSC trees.

cases.prompt: Lighthouse says we're green but users still report the site feels slow. How can analytics help close that gap?
expectations: Reports real-user Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS, plus FCP/TTFB) through the same track() fan-out.
Uses the same metrics and thresholds as the lighthouse skill: LCP <= 2500, INP <= 200, CLS <= 0.1.
Calls reportWebVitals() once on the client and includes name, value, rating, and id.
Explains lab-green + field-poor reveals a gap between test conditions and real devices/networks.

cases.prompt: I want Firebase Analytics on both my web app and my Expo app without forking all my tracking code. What's the approach?
expectations: Uses one adapter shape over Firebase's shared logEvent(name, params) contract, with web and native variants resolved by file extension (.web.ts / .native.ts) or a Platform.OS switch.
On web, lazily imports firebase/analytics behind a browser-only init (initFirebaseAnalytics) so the adapter stays synchronous and SSR-safe.
On native, guards the @react-native-firebase/analytics module instead of window.
Leaves the taxonomy, track() fan-out, consent gate, and useAnalytics hook unchanged across platforms.
